name: Chip
description: A compact pill for filters and choices. Chips can be switched on and off, work as single or multiple choice, or be removable when they stand for filters that are applied.

classes.ayy-chip: A <label> around a native <input type="checkbox"> or radio (which stays in the page but draws nothing), or a <button aria-pressed>. On when the input is checked or aria-pressed="true".
classes.ayy-chip--sm: Small: a step under the default (24px compact), sm text, tighter padding. For a dense toolbar.
classes.ayy-chip--lg: Large: a medium control tall (32px compact), md text, more padding. For a main filter row or touch.
classes.ayy-chip--removable: An active filter: a <span> with its text and an __remove button. Not a control itself.
classes.ayy-chip__count: Number of results after the label, muted, tabular digits.
classes.ayy-chip__remove: The remove (×) button of a removable chip. Needs an aria-label ("Remove Status: Open").
classes.ayy-chip-group: Wrapping row of chips: role="group" with an aria-label, or role="radiogroup" for radio chips.
classes.ayy-chip-group--scroll: One line that scrolls sideways instead of wrapping (a phone toolbar).

default.looks: Pill with a line-strong border, transparent fill, text-soft label at the sm control height.

hover.looks: Wash fill, line-hover border, full text colour. A removable chip keeps its border; its × gets a wash-hover circle.

pressed.none: No pressed look; it toggles on release.

focus.looks: 2px ring, 2px offset (1px on the remove button).

selected.looks: Text-colour border, wash-hover fill and a tick before the label (not colour alone); the count turns text-soft. Forced colours: Highlight fill.

error.none: Chips are filters and choices; show validation on the group with a FieldError.

loading.none: Filtering shows its loading in the results (Skeleton), not on the chip.

scale.sm: Control sm height minus 4px (24px compact, 28 comfortable, 36 touch), control sm text minus 1px, 8px side padding.
scale.md: Control sm height (28px compact, 32 comfortable, 40 touch), control sm text, 12px side padding.
scale.lg: Control md height (32px compact, 40 comfortable, 44 touch), control md text, 16px side padding.

sizes.density: Every size follows data-density with the control scale.
sizes.width: Hugs its label. A group wraps; scroll keeps one line that scrolls sideways (phone toolbars).

js: chipClass({ size?, removable?, className? }), chipGroupClass({ scroll?, className? }) → string; chipCountClass, chipRemoveClass constants; chipRemoveIcon (SVG markup of the cross).

react.import: import { Chip, ChipButton, ChipRemovable, ChipGroup } from "@danitesler/ayywi/react";

props.type: "checkbox" (filters that combine) | "radio" (one choice; same name in the group)
props.name: string

props.scroll: boolean — one line that scrolls sideways

a11y: Checkbox and radio chips are native inputs: Space toggles, radios in a group move with the arrow keys, and screen readers announce "checked". Button chips announce "pressed".
Give the group an aria-label naming what it filters ("Status"), and radio chips role="radiogroup".
The on state is a border, a wash and a tick, not colour alone; High Contrast fills it with the system highlight.
Every remove button needs an aria-label with the filter it removes. After removing one, move focus to the next chip or the search field so it isn't lost.
do: Use chips to filter a list, a table or a grid by a few known values (status, priority, category), with counts when they help.
Use checkbox chips when filters combine, radio chips for one category at a time, ChipButton when the app filters on every click without a form.
Show the filters in force as removable chips above the results, with a Clear all button.
Use ChipGroup scroll in a phone toolbar so the chips stay on one line.
dont: Don't use chips for a status label that can't be clicked — use a Badge.
Don't use chips to switch views or date ranges — use a Segmented control; for navigation between pages use Tabs or links.
Don't show more than eight or so chips in a row — move the rest into a Popover with checkboxes ("More filters").
Don't make a removable chip's whole body the remove target; only the × removes it.
